sentences.text: The genus name Stemec comes from the Coast Salish language, meaning an indefinite long-necked black waterbird native to the discovery area. The species name suntokum honors the family name of the discoverers, Leah and Graham Suntok.

Stemec was a relatively small plotopterid, similar in size to its Miocene relative Plotopterum. The holotype coracoid measures 74.8 mm in length and 12.8 mm in width, though erosion has damaged part of its surface.

The first remains of plotopterids from the Sooke Formation were discovered in 2013 near Sooke by Leah and Graham Suntok. Gary Kaiser, Junya Watanabe, and Marji Johns described the new species Stemec suntokum in 2015.
Fossils found in coastal deposits suggest that the smallest plotopterids like Stemec had coastal habits, unlike larger, older relatives that were pelagic feeders.
Stemec's osteology suggests it was not a proficient swimmer like larger relatives, which may explain why smaller plotopterids survived while larger ones did not.
Stemec fossils are found in the Late Oligocene Sooke Formation of British Columbia. Stemec lived between 27.3 and 23.04 million years ago during the Chattian stage.
